label: Aquinas, I q.14 a.4 co.: God’s act of understanding is his very being
interpretation: Understanding remains in the one who understands. Aquinas argues that a distinct intellectual act would actualize the divine substance as a potency. In divine self-understanding the essence itself is the intelligible species by which God understands. The essence, the object understood and the act of understanding are identical in this case.
attribution: The passage states that in God the act of understanding is identical with his essence and his act of being, which is the premise.
